prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Houston. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Houston for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
For Houston, I’d call **at least three offices**—one academic/multispecialty option and two surgical implant groups—before committing. The best choice depends on whether this is a straightforward single tooth or whether you need extraction, bone grafting, sinus lift, multiple implants, or have medical issues.

### 1. UT Dentists / UTHealth Houston School of Dentistry — Texas Medical Center
**Why call:** This is the strongest “second-opinion” and complex-case option. UTHealth has oral and maxillofacial surgery, periodontics, and prosthodontics in the same institution, so they can coordinate the surgical implant placement and the final crown/bridge.

**Especially worth considering if you:**
- Need a tooth extracted and replaced
- May need bone grafting or a sinus lift
- Have diabetes, take blood thinners, smoke, grind your teeth, or have a history of failed implants
- Want a treatment plan reviewed by specialists rather than a single general office

**Tradeoff:** It may be less convenient, appointments can take longer, and teaching-clinic scheduling is sometimes slower. Ask whether you would be treated in a faculty practice, resident clinic, or specialty clinic, and who performs each step.

---

### 2. Houston Oral Surgery Associates — Houston-area offices
**Why call:** An oral-and-maxillofacial-surgery group is a sensible choice for the **surgical side** of an implant case—especially extractions, grafting, sedation, impacted teeth, or medically complicated cases. Their surgeons focus on surgical planning rather than trying to make every part of the case fit a general-dentistry workflow.

**Especially worth considering if you:**
- Need IV sedation
- Need several teeth removed or implants placed
- Have limited bone, infection, or a previously failed implant
- Want a surgeon to assess whether an implant is even the best option

**Ask:** “Who will design the final tooth/crown plan before the implant is placed?” The implant position should be planned around the final crown, not simply placed where bone happens to be available.

---

### 3. Texas Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants — Houston-area offices
**Why call:** Another good surgical-consult option for implant placement, grafting, extraction, and sedation. Calling a second oral-surgery group is useful because implant recommendations can differ materially—one surgeon may recommend grafting or staged treatment while another may identify a simpler approach.

**Especially worth considering if you:**
- Want to compare a surgical plan and price against Houston Oral Surgery Associates
- Are considering “teeth in a day,” All-on-4–style full-arch work, or multiple implants
- Need an extraction and implant plan coordinated from the start

**Ask:** Whether the quoted implant fee includes the **implant body, abutment, final crown/bridge, CBCT scan, grafting, temporary tooth, sedation, and follow-up visits.** Many advertised implant prices cover only the surgical implant, not the finished tooth.

---

## My practical shortlist

If this is a **single missing tooth with no obvious complications**:
1. UT Dentists/UTHealth for a benchmark plan or prosthodontic opinion  
2. Houston Oral Surgery Associates  
3. Texas Center for Oral Surgery & Dental Implants  
4. Also ask your regular dentist whether they work with a **board-certified prosthodontist** for the crown/implant plan.

If you need **full-mouth, multiple implants, major grafting, or have had implant problems before**, put **UTHealth** at the top of the list and get two specialist opinions before paying a deposit.

---

## What to ask every office when you call

Use this script:

> “I’m looking at a dental implant for [one tooth / multiple teeth]. Do you provide a CBCT-based implant consultation? Who places the implant, who makes the final crown, and can I get an itemized written estimate including grafting, abutment, crown, temporary tooth, sedation, and follow-ups?”

Also ask:

- Is the implant provider a **board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeon** or **board-certified periodontist**?
- Is the final restoration done by a prosthodontist or an experienced restorative dentist?
- Which implant system do you use, and will the parts be readily available in the future?
- What happens if the implant does not integrate or fails early?
- Will I receive copies of the X-rays/CBCT and the treatment plan?
- Do you bill dental insurance, and do you offer financing?
- Can I see the total out-of-pocket cost—not only the surgery fee?

A typical Houston single-tooth implant case can vary widely, but the true all-in total is often roughly **$3,500–$6,500+** once the implant, abutment, crown, imaging, and any grafting are included. Full-arch cases are a completely different price category.

Before booking, verify current locations, participating providers, insurance status, and who will personally perform your procedure; staffing and office arrangements can change.
